schema_notes.tokens: expect values carry {root} (the case root) and {probe} (<root>/probe.sh); the counter reverses {root} onto its own root before comparing
schema_notes.path: list of PATH entries used verbatim (after {root} substitution) joined by ':'; "" is an empty PATH entry (current directory), "." is a dot entry; [] and [""] both give PATH="" (one empty entry = the current directory; measured identical labels); null means PATH absent from the probe environment, so g_find_program_for_path uses its unset default "/bin:/usr/bin:." (gutils.c:370-382). The path-default-* class is the one that reaches that default: both r99 path-unset cases carry an absolute Exec, which returns before the PATH source is read.
schema_notes.modes: optional {rel: octal} map; named files are written with that mode instead of the contract's 0755
schema_notes.rel_desktop: the probe ran `gio launch case.desktop` (relative argument, cwd = the case root); gio canonicalises the desktop argument (gio-tool-launch.c:78), so env_gdf freezes the canonical absolute path as measured
schema_notes.args_rel: the probe passed the args verbatim (relative); frozen argv is post g_file_new_for_commandline_arg as measured
schema_notes.launch_cwd: the probe ran gio with cwd = the case root, so an empty or absent Path= inherits <root>; the counter's candidate leg must run with cwd = <root>
schema_notes.causes: construction first (no-exec; desktop-file = GKeyFile refusal incl. a bad Exec escape, M98-3; exec-parse = shell-level failure, unbalanced quote), then stderr (load, no-terminal, cwd-failed, program-not-found)
schema_notes.multi_spawn: argv lists for multi-spawn cases are frozen sorted; spawn completion order is not observable (M98-10)
schema_notes.desktop_render: case.desktop rendered at 0644, key order Type,Name,Exec,TryExec,Path,Terminal,Hidden,X-GIO-NoFuse, values {root}/{probe} substituted
schema_notes.path_default: path-default-* cases depend on two host facts re-measured 2026-11-08 on glib2 2.90.1-1: /bin is a symlink to /usr/bin, and the TryExec name of the path-default-sysbin class (/usr/bin/sh, cross-checked with /usr/bin/xauth) is executable there and absent from every case root. TryExec is resolved at load time through the same g_find_program_for_path, so the class separates "present in the system dirs" from "not found" without executing a host program: only the case's own probe is ever spawned. The load gate resolves Exec and TryExec with cwd = the case root, and the oracle always runs there.
